stimulus.text: "Take up the White Man's burden — Send forth the best ye breed — Go bind your sons to exile To serve your captives' need; To wait in heavy harness, On fluttered folk and wild — Your new-caught, sullen peoples, Half-devil and half-child. Take up the White Man's burden — In patience to abide, To veil the threat of terror And check the show of pride; By open speech and simple, An hundred times made plain To seek another's profit, And work another's gain." — Rudyard Kipling, "The White Man's Burden," McClure's Magazine, February 1899

source: original; stimulus is a verbatim excerpt (first two stanzas) from Rudyard Kipling, "The White Man's Burden," McClure's Magazine, February 1899, public domain.
stem: Which of Kipling's phrases would an anti-imperialist most directly challenge?

options.misconception: This line is about who goes overseas. An anti-imperialist would challenge the mission itself, not the choice of who carries it out.
This line describes how rule should be carried out. The deeper challenge is to the idea that these peoples need ruling at all.
This line is about repeating the message. It is not the claim an anti-imperialist would attack first.

rationales.A: This line is about who goes overseas. An anti-imperialist would challenge the mission itself, not the choice of who carries it out.
rationales.B: The phrase ranks Filipinos as half-devil and half-child. Background: anti-imperialists rejected the claim that some peoples were unfit to govern themselves.
rationales.C: This line describes how rule should be carried out. The deeper challenge is to the idea that these peoples need ruling at all.
rationales.D: This line is about repeating the message. It is not the claim an anti-imperialist would attack first.
rationales.general:
1. Ask what an anti-imperialist denies. The League denied that Filipinos were unfit to govern themselves.
2. Find the phrase that asserts the opposite. "Half-devil and half-child" says they are unfit, in Kipling's own words.
3. Test the other lines. Each is about method or messengers, not about whether the peoples need ruling.
4. Put it together. The fight turns on the description of the ruled, because the description does the justifying.
Remember: to find the contested claim, look for the words that do the work of justifying the policy.
